questions.q: What are the three layers of monitoring covered in this lesson?
options: Operational metrics, evaluation metrics, and tracing
Billing, licensing, and support tickets
Marketing, sales, and customer service
CPU temperature, fan speed, and disk space
questions.explain: The three layers are operational metrics (token usage, latency, run success), evaluation metrics (coherence, fluency, groundedness), and tracing (the full execution path of a request).

questions.q: According to the lesson's rules of thumb, what does latency above 10 seconds usually signal?
options: Nothing of concern — it's always normal
Model throttling, a slow tool call, or a network issue
That the Azure subscription has expired
That the model needs to be retrained
questions.explain: High latency above 10 seconds is flagged as a signal of throttling, slow tool calls, or network issues worth investigating.

questions.q: What run success rate threshold is called out as worth investigating?
options: Below 95%
Below 10%
Exactly 100%
There is no meaningful threshold
questions.explain: A run success rate below 95% is flagged as worth investigating the failed runs directly.

questions.q: What does the Monitor settings panel let you configure?
options: Only the color theme of the dashboard
Your Azure subscription's billing address
Operational metrics, continuous evaluation, scheduled evaluations, red team scans, and alerts
The physical location of the datacenter
questions.explain: The Monitor settings panel is where you turn on and configure operational metrics, continuous evaluation, scheduled evaluations, red team scans, and alerts.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between a scheduled evaluation and a continuous evaluation?
options: There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A scheduled evaluation only works on weekends
A continuous evaluation requires manually triggering each run
A scheduled evaluation runs on a fixed recurrence, while a continuous evaluation samples live traffic as it happens
questions.explain: A scheduled evaluation runs on a fixed recurrence (e.g., daily at 9 a.m.) against a dataset, while a continuous evaluation samples live production traffic as it occurs.
